newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 10.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$16.84 (+0.06)

The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd (BHP) faces another six to 12 months of difficulty and is likely to underperform for the rest of calendar 1996, brokerage J.B. Were and Son said. In a research report dated August 1996, the brokerage recommended investors' share portfolios be underweight in BHP stock in the short term, but said profits and the group's share price were likely to pick up from 1997.
* The Seven Network Ltd A$3.75 (-0.06)

Seven Network Ltd said late on Monday the advertising market was fairly "tough" but the group was meeting its budget targets. "It's a fairly tough market but we are going all right. We are on track for our budgets," Seven managing director Gary Rice told Reuters in a telephone interview. Seven reported earlier on Monday a jump in net profit to A$115.13 million in the year to June 30 from A$41.26 million in 1994/95.
* North Ltd A$3.75 (+0.05)

North Ltd and MIM Ltd's Argentinian joint venture is one of three bidders for a 230-square-km gold prospect owned by Argentine firm Yacimientos Mineros Aguas de Dionisio (YMAD), YMAD president Americo Timonieri said on Monday.
* Portman Mining Ltd A$1.80 (+0.08)
Portman Mining posted a A$230,000 net profit for the first half of the 1996 year late on Monday, up from a A$4.18 million loss the previous corresponding half year.
* Newcrest Mining Ltd A$4.63 (+0.03)

Newcrest Mining Ltd said late on Monday that ore processed at its newly-approved Cadia mine in central western New South Wales might potentially rise to more than 20 million tonnes a year from a planned 17 million.
* Davids Ltd A$1.69 (+0.03)

Davids Ltd is expected to report stronger full year results later on Tuesday. Analysts forecast Davids' year after-tax pre-abnormal earnings to rise 17.5 percent to about A$53.6 million, from A$45.6 million in the year to June 30, 1995.
* Equatorial Mining NL A$0.155 (+0.005)

Minera El Tesoro, a Chilean/Australian joint venture, will start a feasibility study this year for a 60,000 tonne copper mine at its deposit in the northern Atacama Desert, said officials on Monday. El Tesoro is owned 61 percent by Chile's Luksic group with Equatorial Mining NL holding 39 percent.
* Johnson's Well Mining NL A$4.00 (unch)

Joseph Gutnick's Johnson's Well Mining NL said on Monday it has reached a joint venture agreement with Australian mining identity Mark Creasy over an exploration license in the Duken belt near Laveton in Western Australia.

Gold miner Devex Ltd said late on Monday its objective is to increase its gold resources to more than one million ounces within two years by stepping up exploration. The company earlier on Monday reported net profit of A$5.14 million in 1995/1996, up from A$3.81 million in the previous year.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
